newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close down aas profit takers move in.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close down aas profit takers move in.

text.p: The Stockholm bourse closed lower on Wednesday, ending two consecutive days of record high closes, as profit takers moved into the market.
The Stockholm general index closed 0.29 percent lower at 2,462.89 after a fairly active day's trading in which shares worth 5.50 billion crowns changed hands.
"There is definitely a certain amount of profit taking particularly in shares that have gone up a lot lately," said one broker.
Telecoms company Ericsson was well traded and slipped 2.5 crowns to 233 crowns after hitting a record high recently.
Drugs major Astra also posted losses, closing 1.5 crowns weaker at 330 crowns. Astra said its U.S. Losec sales would not be threatened by sales of Proctor & Gamble's new gastric ulcer treatment.

Fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz finally ended a bull run prompted by rumours of a share split and about its fourth quarter earnings that took it to new highs of 1,175 crowns this week and closed 15 crowns lower at 1,120 crowns.
The forestry sector weakened, slipping 1.12 percent. Swedish forestry cooperative Sodra said NorScan stocks were largely unchanged in December.
